newsitem.title: USA: Orange County D.A. to drop Merrill Lynch probe.
newsitem.headline: Orange County D.A. to drop Merrill Lynch probe.

text.p: The district attorney's office of Orange County, Calif., on Thursday will drop its long-running investigation of Merrill Lynch & Co. in exchange for a payment of about $30 million, sources close to the probe said.
As part of the settlement, Merrill Lynch will deny any wrongdoing, the sources said.
The district attorney plans to hold a news conference at 11 a.m. local time (2 p.m. EDT) to make the announcement. County prosecutors declined to comment in advance.
An Orange County grand jury has been investigating the roles played by various bond and investment firms, including Merrill Lynch, and other finance professionals in the county's bankruptcy crisis.
The grand jury focused on Merrill Lynch's role as the underwriter of county notes. The panel's deliberations have been kept secret, but rumors spread in recent weeks that indictments were likely.
Merrill Lynch declined to comment on the district attorney's settlement.
Orange County shocked Wall Street in December 1994 when it filed for bankruptcy after losing more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy one year ago.

To recover the funds it lost, the county filed a $2-billion-plus lawsuit against Merrill Lynch alleging it sold the county risky securities in violation of state law. Merrill Lynch has denied any wrongdoing and has been contesting the county's lawsuit in court.
Sources said Merrill Lynch's settlement with the district attorney would not have any impact on the county's lawsuit against the investment bank.
